authority_levels.approve: Executor posts the step and waits for an analyst to approve it.
authority_levels.recommend_only: Executor writes the step into the plan and never dispatches it.

eradication.note: The analyst executes these through the action surface, so the framework still times the phase and MTTE stays measured.

recovery.note: reverse_only_live_actions keeps recovery off entries the ledger recorded as shadow, which never happened and so cannot be undone.

rules.name: malicious_high_confidence
rules.reason: Assessment returned a malicious verdict at high confidence

elevate.note: Any matching rule elevates the case; conditions inside a rule are AND'd via `requires`. Deliberately conservative - a star cannot be undone by the framework and a starred case is exempt from auto-close, so the bar is a malicious verdict at high confidence. escalate_recommended was removed as a star condition: the prompt itself warns it must not merely restate the verdict, and on a Turla Carbon replay it was true on 53 of 60 assessed issues against 48 malicious - so it only ever loosened the bar, adding one case that had no malicious issue at all. Measured on that replay, malicious-at-high-confidence starred exactly the five cases carrying real attack activity and left the unrelated AIRS and AWS findings alone. raise_severity ships FALSE: the severity action is not shipped yet because its placeholders do not resolve from context written in the same run. Starring is unaffected. When severity lands it is RAISE ONLY - the framework never lowers one. An absent field never matches. Operators: eq, in, gte.

emergency.note: Issue-level containment that does not wait for the case. SOCFWEmergencyResponse runs the containment actions of every policy an issue matches, once each, as issue_emergency; only containment actions are allowed. about matches the issue's product category. A host action runs only on a host that is not protected and is either in containable_hosts (when that is set) or has a role in containable_roles (any turns the role check off). The role comes from, first to answer: this tenant's role entries, the EDR (SOCFramework.Endpoint.role), the operating system (macOS and Windows client editions read as workstation, Windows Server as server, Linux as unknown). An unknown role is never contained. A host the EDR already reports contained or pending is skipped. Containment that was needed but blocked by these rules stars the case and raises its severity to escalate_severity (raise only), as automation. Every action ships shadowed, so in a PoV this records what would have been contained. The issue is closed as true positive, contained (soc-close-issue-contained, as automation) only when every action really ran. Entries in protect and containable_hosts are host:<name or pattern>, ip:<address>, cidr:<range>, account:<name or pattern> or list:<XSIAM list name>, one entry per line; role entries are host:<pattern>:<role>. A tenant replaces any of these with !SOCFWConfig command=emergency; rule_id and name_contains belong in tenant policies only.

ticketing.note: Ticket scope is the case. Per-issue tickets rebuild the alert storm that case grouping exists to remove.
